titleText.es: Según oigo, muchos de vosotros ya tenéis Flash fluido, pero yo y mi tarjeta Intel seguimos esperando un parche del kernel en algún punto de la pipeline para poder ver a Jon Stewart con fluidez.
titleText.en: I hear many of you finally have smooth Flash support, but me and my Intel card are still waiting on a kernel patch somewhere in the pipeline before we can watch Jon Stewart smoothly.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive and official xkcd source both identify comic #619. The archive translates the official title text while retaining the product and platform names Flash and Intel.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Trabajo often means work or a job. In costar trabajo, it instead names the effort or difficulty involved in doing something.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: support; technical ability to work with something
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In technology, soporte can mean that a system is compatible with a device, format, or feature, not only help from a support worker.

example.es: El navegador tiene soporte para este formato.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: for; introduces what technical support covers or enables
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After soporte, para can introduce a device, format, feature, or action that the system can work with.

example.es: La aplicación incluye soporte para exportar audio.
example.en: The application includes support for exporting audio.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In computing, a procesador is the hardware that carries out program instructions. Procesadores is plural.
A límite can be a boundary or the greatest allowed value. In technical descriptions, it often names the maximum a system supports.

example.es: El límite del sistema es de cien usuarios.
example.en: The system limit is one hundred users.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you all have (informal plural, mainly Spain)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tenéis is the present form of tener for vosotros or vosotras. It informally addresses more than one person and is used especially in Spain.

example.en: Do you all have the tickets?

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ya often means ‘already.’ In a question about an expected change, natural English commonly uses ‘yet’ or ‘by now.’

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to play; to play back audio or video
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With audio or video, reproducir means to play the media. In other settings it can mean to reproduce, copy, or recreate something.

example.es: Pulsa aquí para reproducir el vídeo.
example.en: Press here to play the video.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Vídeos is the plural of vídeo. The form with stress on ví- is standard in Spain; video without the written accent is common in much of Latin America.

example.es: Guardé los vídeos en el ordenador.
example.en: I saved the videos on the computer.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins a pantalla completa, ‘full-screen’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The display expression uses a before pantalla completa. Translate the complete expression rather than a by itself.

example.es: Abrió el mapa a pantalla completa.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In pantalla completa, completa matches the feminine singular noun pantalla and says that the content uses the whole screen.

example.es: La presentación está a pantalla completa.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Fluida describes something that moves or works without interruptions. In de forma fluida, it matches the feminine noun forma while the full expression describes how an action happens.

example.es: La animación se reproduce de forma fluida.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you say that doing something is difficult or takes effort?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of costar followed by trabajo; mucho can emphasize the amount of effort.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Costar changes for the time and for what is difficult: cuesta trabajo now and costó trabajo for a completed past situation. A person affected can appear with me, te, le, nos, os, or les.

example.en: Organizing it takes us a lot of effort.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you name the device, format, feature, or action that a system supports?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use soporte para, then name the supported thing or use an action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A noun can follow para, as in soporte para impresoras. For a supported action, use an unchanged -ar, -er, or -ir verb: soporte para imprimir.

example.es: El programa añade soporte para cámaras nuevas.
example.en: The program adds support for new cameras.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that content is displayed using the whole screen?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pantalla is feminine, so completa uses feminine singular -a. The preposition a remains fixed in this display expression.

example.es: Vimos la película a pantalla completa.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: Linux · miles de procesadores · vídeo Flash fluido
cardDefinitions.questionEn: What contrast creates the joke about the patch's supported features?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: The patch supports an unusually specialized machine with thousands of processors, yet the user still cannot smoothly play ordinary full-screen Flash video. The developer celebrates impressive large-scale engineering while dismissing the everyday feature the other person actually wants.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Linux is an operating-system family. Flash was a widely used web-media platform when the comic appeared in 2009, and smooth video playback depended on practical graphics, driver, and software support rather than merely accepting a huge processor count.

applications.explanationEn: Costó places the difficulty in completed past time, mucho strengthens the amount, and trabajo names the effort involved.
Último comes before parche and uses masculine singular -o to match it; here it identifies the most recent patch.
Soporte names technical compatibility, para introduces what is supported, and máquinas fills that device slot.

applications.explanationEn: The -éis ending marks the several people addressed informally in the vosotros form used mainly in Spain.
In this question about an expected feature, ya asks whether it is available yet or by now.
Soporte names compatibility, para introduces the supported action, and reproducir remains in its unchanged dictionary form.
A begins the fixed display expression, pantalla names the screen, and completa says that the whole screen is used.
Completa follows the noun pantalla in the ordinary descriptive order.
Completa uses feminine singular -a to match the feminine singular noun pantalla.
De forma introduces how the playback happens, and fluida describes that manner while matching the feminine noun forma.
Fluida follows the noun forma in the ordinary descriptive order.
Fluida uses feminine singular -a to match the feminine singular noun forma.
